comment: The Trino figure is the report's "official" number, not a run on the same hardware as StarRocks.
evidence: Section 6.3 summary table, SF1000 on Iceberg/GCS: StarRocks 4.0.8 (4 CN, warm) geomean 2.198s vs Trino 475 geomean 6.782s; Trino figure is the page's 'official' number, not a same-hardware run.

SF100 raw hot runtime, hardware-matched sizes named in the post: Snowflake Large Gen2 15.9s, ClickHouse Cloud 59-core node 19.8s, BigQuery 2,000 slots 26.2s, Databricks Large 28.9s, Redshift Serverless 128 RPU 30.7s.

comment: Our calculation from raw results published by Polars. Query 18 is excluded because DataFusion ran out of memory on it.
evidence: Computed from raw results in github.com/pola-rs/polars-2.0-benchmark, SF100 on c7a.4xlarge, sum of best-of-5 over 21 queries (q18 excluded, DataFusion OOM): Polars 2.0 34.6s, DuckDB 1.5.6 50.2s, DataFusion 54 78.0s. DuckDB 2.0 alpha not counted.

comment: Our calculation from raw results published by Polars. Queries 67 and 72 are excluded because DataFusion timed out.
evidence: Computed from raw results in github.com/pola-rs/polars-2.0-benchmark, SF100 on c7a.4xlarge, sum of best-of-5 over 97 queries (q67, q72 excluded, DataFusion timeouts): Polars 2.0 85.8s, DuckDB 1.5.6 112.7s, DataFusion 54 198.5s. DuckDB 2.0 alpha not counted.

comment: SF-100 result. At the smaller SF-10 size the top two swap: Polars streaming beats DuckDB.
evidence: Republished 'Updated PDS-H benchmark results (May 2025)', SF-100 total_time table: DuckDB 1.3.0 19.65s, Polars 1.30 streaming 23.94s (in-memory 152.27s not counted separately), PySpark 4.0 312.43s, Dask 2025.5.1 548.52s. At SF-10 Polars streaming is first (3.89s vs DuckDB 5.87s).

comment: The page has no publication date; we use the release date of the newest version tested.
evidence: Rerun on the same docs page, SSB-Flat 100 GB, SUM row of the Test results table: StarRocks 3.5.0 992ms, ClickHouse 25.3.3.42 1858ms, Apache Druid 33.0.0 4710ms. Page has no publication date; date is the release date of the newest tested build (StarRocks 3.5.0, 2025-06-13).

comment: A TPC-DS-inspired set of 85 queries, run once from cold. First and second place are under 3% apart.
evidence: README results table, TPC-DS-inspired 85-query cohort at ~SF3000 (3 TB), single cold pass run 2026-10-11..13; ranked by batch time, the author's primary metric: Fabric Warehouse 23.35 min, Snowflake optimized 23.98 min, Azure Databricks Photon 47.34 min (geomean gives the same order). One lane per product: Fabric Lakehouse endpoint, Snowflake baseline, Databricks non-Photon and the unranked Fabric Spark notebook not counted.

comment: Published by Exasol about its own product. ClickHouse is left out because it completed only 18 of 22 queries. Trino's last place comes from the text, not a listed time.
evidence: Exasol-authored. Concurrency series, 1 node, SF50, 1 stream, median of 5 runs, totals from the text: Exasol 22.4s, DuckDB 81.5s, StarRocks 87.4s; Trino placed last from the text stating it is slowest in every configuration (its 1-stream total is only in Figure 1). ClickHouse left out: it completed only 18 of 22 queries (95.5s over the subset).

comment: Analyst article favourable to Oracle that doesn't say who ran the test. Transaction speed was equal, so the analytics half decides. One of its throughput sentences appears to swap the two figures.
evidence: Analyst article on Oracle's MySQL HeatWave launch, vendor-favourable; it does not name who ran the test. CH-benCHmark 100G: OLTP equal (0.02 s latency, 30K transactions/min for both), so the OLAP side decides: 4 concurrent OLAP sessions, HeatWave 35 s vs Aurora db.r5.8xlarge 632 s latency (18x). The OLAP throughput sentence claims 110x for HeatWave but prints .06 for HeatWave and 6.6 for Aurora, apparently swapped.

comment: HEAVY.AI timed out on 37 of 113 queries. Each counts as the 120 s limit, so its real time would be longer.
evidence: UC Merced technical report, section 5.6 and Table 6, total time for the 113 JOB queries with each engine's default optimizer, no indexes, same CPU server: DuckDB 30.38s, MonetDB 114.46s, HEAVY.AI 4744s (37 queries hit the 120s timeout, each charged as 120s, so a lower bound). Forced-join-order (no-CE) runs not counted; PostgreSQL left out because the paper runs it tuned, with a different timeout, and does not tabulate it against these three.

comment: DuckDB ran embedded and the others in Docker. PostgreSQL had 23 extra indexes. The report has no publication date; we use the commit that added it.
evidence: New-suite measurements table, rows "JOB, original snapshot", all 113 queries, result hashes matching across engines, M4 Pro, 10 threads, 24 GiB: sum of query medians DuckDB 3.30s, StarRocks 7.24s, ClickHouse 13.92s, MonetDB 20.15s, PostgreSQL 73.36s (with 23 foreign-key indexes); the geometric-mean ratio gives the same order. DuckDB runs embedded, the others in Docker. Date is the commit that added the report.

comment: BenchBox does not rank these runs. Local engines ran on an Apple M4 laptop, cloud warehouses over the network. Polars' results were not validated. By total time SQLite would fall behind Polars.
evidence: BenchBox Results table, JOB SF 1, power phase, 113 queries, geomean query time: DuckDB 76 ms, ClickHouse Local 122 ms, SQLite 131 ms, Polars 262 ms, DataFusion 280 ms, Snowflake (X-Small) 634 ms, Databricks 1.93 s, BigQuery 3.48 s. DuckDB is the untuned run, like the rest (the tuned run, 55 ms, gives the same order). By total time SQLite would fall behind Polars. Caveats: the site marks all 9 runs "not ranked"; local engines ran on an Apple M4 laptop, cloud ones over the network from it; the Polars run has no result validation. Runs date from 2026-08-25 to 2026-10-03; date is the newest run.

comment: BenchBox does not rank these runs. Local engines ran on an Apple M4, cloud warehouses over the network, where fixed overhead dominates at this small size. Polars and Pandas results were not validated.
evidence: BenchBox Results table, SSB SF 1 (the scale with the most engines), power phase, 13 queries, untuned runs, geomean query time: DuckDB 6.8 ms, DataFusion 22 ms, Polars 41 ms, ClickHouse Local 67 ms, Snowflake (X-Small) 388 ms, Databricks (2X-Small) 827 ms, BigQuery 869 ms, Pandas 2.51 s, SQLite 3.29 s. Caveats: the site marks all 10 runs "not ranked" (no Power@Size); local engines ran on an Apple M4, cloud ones over the network from it, where fixed per-query overhead dominates (BigQuery is flagged "timing-plateau"); Polars and Pandas runs have no result validation. Runs date from 2026-08-25 to 2026-10-03; date is the newest run.

comment: Only the runs BenchBox itself ranks; other engines' runs were non-standard, incomplete or defective. DuckDB and Spark ran on an Apple M4, cloud warehouses over the network.
evidence: BenchBox Results table, TPC-DS SF 1, power phase, 103 queries, only the runs BenchBox itself ranks (6 of 20): DuckDB 13 ms geomean (Power@Size 269,803; its two other ranked runs, 32 and 45 ms, also lead), Spark 557 ms (6,211), Snowflake X-Small 974 ms (3,709), Databricks 2X-Small 1.35 s (2,765); both measures give this order. DataFusion, ClickHouse Local, Polars, Pandas, BigQuery and SQLite are left out because BenchBox excludes their runs as non-standard, incomplete or known defective (superseded SQL translation). DuckDB and Spark ran locally on an Apple M4, the cloud warehouses over the network. Date is the newest ranked run.

comment: Known defect: BenchBox's data generator wrote bad addresses, so 4 of 22 queries return wrong values, and BenchBox does not rank these runs. Kept until it publishes reruns. Local engines ran on an Apple M4, cloud warehouses over the network.
evidence: BenchBox Results table, TPC-H SF 1, power phase, 22 queries, untuned standard runs (Apple M4 for local engines), geomean query time: DuckDB 35 and 38 ms, Polars 36 and 37 ms (repeat runs interleave, so a tie), DataFusion 47 ms, ClickHouse Local 70 ms, SQLite 494 ms, Spark SQL 719 ms, Snowflake X-Small 943 ms, Databricks 2X-Small 956 ms, BigQuery 1.04 s. Known defect: BenchBox flags all of these runs "known defective data" and does not rank them, because its macOS generator wrote non-canonical addresses, so Q2, Q10, Q15 and Q20 return wrong values (results-data/DEFECTIVE_DATAGEN_AUDIT.md); recorded anyway on the maintainer's decision, to be replaced by BenchBox reruns. Snowflake and Databricks swap places on Power@Size (3,645 vs 3,843). Not counted: non-standard and tuned runs, runs on other machines, PySpark DataFrame and DuckLake. Cloud engines ran over the network. Date is the newest run counted.
